Date: Fri, 10 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: RFI: Data processing agreement annex + cross-border transfer evidence

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks for taking the call yesterday. As part of our vendor due diligence for HealthSys’ new telehealth platform, Procurement asked us to collect detailed DPA annex language and cross-border transfer evidence (DPF/SCCs or adequacy basis). Please could you provide the following:

1) A draft DPA annex (or proposed language) that covers subprocessors, logging/auditability, retention, and data deletion on contract termination.
2) Evidence of transfers outside the EEA/UK: do you rely on the EU-US DPF, SCCs, or other mechanism? Please attach your current transfer impact assessment if available.
3) SOC2 / artifact references and whether logs/audit records can be included in an audit package for a scoped review.
4) Any standard redlines you are unwilling to accept (especially around data residency or deletion holdbacks).

We need this by COB next Thursday (2026-10-15) to feed into our legal review. Happy to schedule a quick follow-up if that helps.

Regards,
Elena Ruiz
Data Protection Officer
HealthSys Medical Group

Subject: Draft: Redwood DPA Annex + transfer assessment (initial)

Team —

Attached is a first-pass DPA annex (Redwood_DPA_Annex_v3.docx) tailored to HealthSys asks. Key callouts in the draft:

- Subprocessors: we enumerate categories and commit to 30 days’ notice for new subprocessors; we accept reasonable objections for high-risk subprocessor additions.
- Data residency: for hosted customers, we offer region-pinning to EEA or US-only clusters; Dedicated/Private deployments are available where customer manages network.
- Transfers: primary lawful basis is SCCs (controller-to-processor modules) with our transfer impact assessment on file. Where customers require, we can implement Dedicated deployments to avoid transfers.
- Logging & auditability: we can provide redacted audit bundles scoped to agreed records; full raw logs require a governance process due to service provider confidentiality.
- Deletion: we commit to deletion of customer content within 30 days of termination unless legal hold is requested; KV cache and backups are described in the annex.

I’ve also prepared a short summary PDF (Redwood_DPF-Assessment-summary.pdf) that explains our transfer risk mitigations (encryption in transit at TLS1.3, rest encryption keys, strict access controls, contractual SCCs, and technical segmentation).

Open items for Elena / HealthSys legal:
- Any contractual language HealthSys requires for data localization (we can accept clear carve-outs but not indefinite on-shore-only mandates for hosted).
- Confirmation whether HealthSys will accept SCCs + our TIA or will require EU-US DPF attestation.

I will mark the draft where we have firm commitments vs. negotiable items. Please review and suggest redlines.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security
Redwood Inference

Marissa —

Thanks for the fast turnaround; we reviewed the annex and uploaded a redline (HealthSys_DPA_Redline_v1.docx). High-level items we flagged:

1) Transfer mechanism: HealthSys legal prefers an adequacy/DPF-based approach for US transfers — can you confirm timing for finalizing Redwood’s DPF attestation? If not available, will SCCs + the TIA be sufficient for an interim contract?
2) Deletion timing: our compliance policy requires deletion within 14 days for certain PHI categories — your 30-day window may be a blocker unless we can scope the retention in the SOW.
3) Audit package: we need SOC2 Type II report and a scoped audit bundle for a 3rd-party review. Please indicate timelines for delivering SOC artifacts.

Can we schedule a 30-minute call tomorrow (Thu 10/15) to resolve the deletion and transfer mechanism? Procurement is aiming to finalize commercial terms next week.

Best,
Elena Ruiz
DPO, HealthSys

Subject: Re: Draft: Redwood DPA Annex + transfer assessment (initial)

Hi Elena / Mark —

Thanks — we reviewed HealthSys’s redline and pulled together a short response set and next-steps in the attached bundle. Summary answers:

• DPF status: Redwood’s EU-US DPF attestation is currently in final internal review and we expect formal attestation in Q4 2026 (target late Nov). Meanwhile, we accept SCCs + our TIA as the interim legal mechanism; we will include a contractual commitment to migrate to DPF once attestation is in place.

• Deletion window: We can offer a mapped SOW commitment: 14-day deletion for scoped PHI fields (as a contract addendum) provided the customer agrees to a short implementation checklist (retention flags + routing to EEA-only). For general content, 30 days remains the standard.

• SOC2 / audit: SOC2 Type II report is available for the last 12-month period; we will provide the report via our secure artifact portal once an NDA and data access agreement are in place. Scoped audit bundles can be produced within 10 business days of a signed review agreement.

Next steps:
1) We attach our redlines and the DPF summary (Redwood_DPA_Annex_v3.docx; Redwood_DPF-Assessment-summary.pdf).
2) Proposed call: Thu 10/15 16:00 ET — confirm or suggest an alternative.
3) If HealthSys accepts SCCs + TIA as interim, we’ll update the draft with the 14-day PHI deletion addendum and circulate for signature.

Appreciate the quick turnaround on your side.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
